meta.description: FLUX.2 Klein 9B character LoRA in the 16 GB laptop memory profile (RTX 5080 Laptop 16 GB, 96 GB system RAM, native Windows - NOBLE-G18), trained at 1024. SOURCE: the memory settings are COMMUNITY-DERIVED 16 GB settings (ostris/ai-toolkit issues #653 and #669, community Klein low-VRAM guides), NOT measured on the laptop and NOT reproduced in this fork - the fork's last laptop record for Klein is an OOM without layer offloading (batchAdvisor LAPTOP16, variant not recorded). Treat the headroom as inferred and run a short test first. TRAINING MATH IS INHERITED UNCHANGED from flux2_klein_9b_character_lora v1.2: LoRA rank 16 / alpha 16, adamw8bit at LR 1e-4, bf16, sigmoid timesteps, batch 1 x accum 1, 1500 steps, caption dropout 0.05 (BFL-published Klein defaults; not 9B-measured). DELTAS, all memory/IO except resolution: (1) resolution [1024] ONLY - the parent's 768 bucket is dropped on purpose (multi-aspect buckets around 1024 stay on). (2) layer_offloading on: text encoder 100%, transformer 80% streamed from system RAM. The fp8 9B transformer is ~9 GB; at 80% about 2 GB stays resident, leaving most of the card for 1024 activations (4096 image tokens) with gradient checkpointing. Community #669 reports a 9B run at 100% offload sitting at ~14.6 GB on a 16 GB card, but that was an edit LoRA with control images (about double the sequence length), so plain character training should have more room - 80% leans high without paying the full 100% speed cost. (3) Text embeddings cached and the text encoder unloaded (cache_text_embeddings + unload_text_encoder), so Mistral is not resident while training; this makes caption dropout a no-op and is mutually exclusive with diff_output_preservation. Latents cached to disk and served from RAM. (4) Sampling DISABLED by default (train.disable_sampling) - on a 16 GB card the sampler, not the training loop, is the VRAM peak. The sample block is kept at 1024 with five [trigger] prompts so you can turn it on, but expect it to spike memory; the intended workflow is train with sampling off, then test the kept checkpoints. max_step_saves_to_keep 10 (save every 250) so every checkpoint of a run up to 2500 steps is kept. QUANTIZATION: quantize + quantize_te with qtype qfloat8 as in the parent - but layer_offloading silently rewrites qfloat8 -> torchao float8 for both (toolkit/config_modules.py ~772-775), so the run will use float8, not quanto qfloat8. That is upstream behaviour, not a preset bug. LOADING (#653): the fork's flux2 load path no longer moves the whole bf16 transformer to the GPU before quantizing - it loads on CPU and quantizes block-by-block on the GPU, then hands the blocks to the layer offloader, so the issue-#653 load-time OOM should not apply (read from code, not tested on 16 GB). WINDOWS: set NVIDIA Control Panel > Manage 3D settings > CUDA - Sysmem Fallback Policy = Prefer No Sysmem Fallback (for the trainer's python.exe or globally). Without it a config grazing the ceiling does not OOM - it spills into shared memory and step time jumps several-fold (#669: ~15 -> 50-90 s/it). If s/it suddenly balloons, you are spilling, not compute-bound. Keep ~1.5 GB VRAM free. IF YOU OOM, in order: (1) confirm sampling is still off; (2) raise layer_offloading_transformer_percent 0.8 -> 1.0; (3) set cache_latents false (keep cache_latents_to_disk) to give back RAM-served latents; (4) only then lower resolution to 768 - that last step changes the recipe. If it fits with headroom, lower the transformer percent toward 0.6 for speed. STEPS: meta.step_table below is the fork's existing Klein 9B rule (60 steps/image, clamped 1000-2500, stepSuggestion.ts ARCH_HEURISTICS) written out as points - 17 images ~1000, 20 ~1200, 30 ~1800, 40 ~2400, 42+ capped at 2500. No fork doc gives a reason to change it at 1024 (BFL's 1500-step starting point and 1000-1750 peak are not resolution-split), so the numbers are deliberately UNCHANGED from the per-arch rule; the panel labels it 'preset step table' and divides by effective batch. Other Klein presets keep the per-arch advisor. BATCH: batch 1 recommended. The Machine: 16 GB laptop plan treats batch 1 as an UNMEASURED attempt when layer_offloading is on (the recorded OOM was without it); effective batch above 1 goes through gradient_accumulation. Set your Trigger Word in the job form; the sample prompts use [trigger]. Gated on HF - accept the licence.
